From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Here's a draft you can adapt:

---

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message. I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee added to my account for this month.

Under Section 4.2 of my lease, rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and "no late fees may be charged during the grace period." My rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period. Because the fee was charged during the grace period, it is not permitted under the lease, and I will not be paying it.

Please remove the $75 charge from my account and confirm in writing that it has been reversed. I'd also ask that you confirm the grace period will be applied to my account in the future.

I'm happy to discuss this further, but I expect the fee to be removed. Please respond by [date, e.g., 7 days from now]. If it isn't resolved, I'll pursue the matter through [local tenant resource / small claims court / my local housing authority, as applicable].

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

Notes:
- Keep a copy of this email and your payment confirmation (the receipt showing the 3rd) in case you need them later.
- The lease language is on your side, so citing Section 4.2 directly is your strongest point.
- If you want a firmer tone, delete the "happy to discuss" line. If you want a softer one, you can drop the final paragraph about next steps, though I'd keep the request for written confirmation.
- Check your local tenant laws too; some areas have additional protections on late fees beyond what's in the lease.

Here's a draft you can adapt:

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message. I'm writing about the $75 late fee added to my account for this month's rent.

Rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within the grace period under Section 4.2 of our lease. That section states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period, which runs through the 5th. Because the fee was applied during that window, it isn't permitted under the lease, and I won't be paying it.

I'd appreciate it if you could remove the $75 charge from my account and confirm in writing that it has been reversed. I'm glad to discuss this further if you see it differently, but I'd ask that you point to the specific lease provision that supports the charge.

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B
[Date]

---

A few notes:

- **Keep proof of the payment date.** If you paid through the resident portal, screenshot the confirmation. If you paid by check or money order, use the postmark, a receipt, or your bank statement showing when it cleared.
- **Send it in writing**, which Section 9.4 permits by email, so you have a dated record.
- **If the fee stays on your account**, you can escalate by requesting a meeting or checking whether your city or state has rules on late fees for residential tenants. Many places cap late fees or require a specific grace period, and a local tenant rights organization can tell you what applies.
